summary: Mikaël Bauer specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Kanazawa University under Paul Hoornaert and Noritoshi Aramaki, and earned a PhD from Harvard University (attested 2010) under Ryuichi Abe.

Mikel Burley works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Essex and Bristol under J. M. Bernstein, Jonardon Ganeri, Brian Carr, and John Peacock, later becoming Associate Professor of Religion and Philosophy at the University of Leeds (attested 2007–2020).
Mikio Otsuki specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held posts as a research fellow at Manpuku-ji and as a professor at Hanazono University (both attested 2007).

Mikisaburo Mori (1909–1986) worked in philosophy and Sinology. Educated at Kyoto and Osaka universities, he held positions at Kyoto University (1935–1947), Osaka High School (1942), Osaka University (1950; 1966–1973), and Bukkyo University (~1973–1984).
Milman Parry (1902–1935) was a scholar in linguistics. He studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Paris under Antoine Meillet, and served on the faculty at Harvard University from ~1929 to 1935.

Milo Cleveland Beach (born 1939) works in Indology and history/archaeology. A Harvard alumnus, he held posts at the Fogg Museum, Boston MFA, Williams College, Arthur M. Sackler Gallery, and served as Director of the National Museum of Asian Art (~1988–2001).
Milton Singer (1912–1994) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Texas at Austin and the University of Chicago, where he later held a post from ~1940 to 1979.
Min Ling Khenchen Tsewang Rigdzin studied under Dilgo Khyentse and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Min Thu Wun (1909–2004) was a scholar in linguistics. He studied at the University of Rangoon (~1927–1935) under Pe Maung Tin and later pursued studies at the University of Oxford (~1936–1939).
Ming Mei specializes in Sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at SOAS under Roderick Whitfield and Andrey Terentyev, and earned an MPhil at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin.

Ming-Wood Liu (born 1947) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. Educated at the University of Hong Kong and UCLA under Kenneth K. S. Ch'en and Robert C. Epp, he was a professor at the University of Hong Kong (~1980–2012).
Mingyu Fu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University (attested 2013) under the supervision of Huifeng Shi.

Minori Nishimura (born 1947) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Taisho University under Shunkyo Katsumata and Seiren Matsunami, later holding positions at Taisho University (attested 2002–2008) and the Sanko Cultural Institute (attested 2002).

Minoru Hara (1930–2021) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Harvard, he taught at the University of Tokyo (1960–1991) and served as President of the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (1996–2006).
Minoru Inaba specializes in history/archaeology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at Kyoto University, including as professor (attested 2011 and 2022).

Minoru Kiyota (1923–2013) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and others, and served as professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965–1994, attested 1998–2004).

Minton Warren (1850–1907) was a linguist who studied at Tufts, Yale under William Dwight Whitney, Leipzig, Bonn, and Strasbourg. He held professorships at Johns Hopkins University (1879–1899) and Harvard University (1899), and led the American Academy in Rome (1896–1899).
Minyak Kunzang Sonam studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

id: P:Minyak Rongsharwa Tubten Lek Shé Zangpo
summary: Minyak Rongsharwa Tubten Lek Shé Zangpo studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Mio Kishimoto (born 1952) specializes in Sinology and history/archaeology. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1971–1979), she held positions at Ochanomizu University (~1981–1994) and the University of Tokyo as professor (~1994–2007).
